question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2023 Q2c — Oxidation Number of Cl in NaClO
question.text:
One of the main active ingredients in chlorine bleach is the oxidising agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaClO). Bleach reacts with water as follows:

NaClO + H₂O → HOCl + NaOH

Deduce the oxidation number of Cl in the formula NaClO. Show your working.
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
Oxidation number rules applied to NaClO:
• Na = +1 (Group I metal — always +1 in compounds)
• O = −2 (oxygen in compounds, standard rule)
• Sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound = 0:
 (+1) + Cl + (−2) = 0
 Cl = 0 − 1 + 2 = +1

Key distractor: Students often confuse this with Cl in NaCl (which is −1). In NaClO, oxygen forces Cl to be positive.

steps.label:
Oxidation number rules:
1. Neutral compound: sum of all oxidation numbers = 0
2. Group I metals (Na, K, Li): always +1 in compounds
3. Oxygen: usually −2 in compounds (except peroxides)
4. Assign unknown element last, using the sum = 0 rule
Assign known oxidation numbers and solve for Cl in NaClO. (3 marks)

fields.label: Oxidation number of Na in NaClO = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Na is a Group I metal — its oxidation number is always +1 in ionic/covalent compounds.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Group I elements (Na, K, Li) always have oxidation number +1 in compounds. So Na = +1.

fields.label: Oxidation number of O in NaClO = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Oxygen has oxidation number −2 in most compounds (except peroxides like H₂O₂ where it is −1).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: In most compounds, oxygen = −2. NaClO is not a peroxide, so O = −2 applies here.

fields.label: Oxidation number of Cl in NaClO = _____

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Set up: (+1) + Cl + (−2) = 0. Solving: Cl = 0 − 1 + 2 = +1. The Cl in bleach is +1, unlike NaCl where Cl is −1.
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Apply: sum of oxidation numbers = 0 for neutral compound. (+1) + Cl + (−2) = 0 → Cl = +1. Don't confuse with Cl in NaCl (which is −1).
